text:
acme_ops: Hey, hitting 429s across our prod cluster starting ~10:03 UTC. No code deploys on our side. We flipped on a websocket heartbeat to keep connections warm and now our integration is failing. Tests show short 429 bursts every few minutes. Anyone seen this pattern?

sara_support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste one or two request IDs or sample headers? Is it streaming responses or short RPCs?

acme_ops: Short RPCs, mostly POST /v1/generate. Sample header from a failed request: 
```
X-Req-Id: 8a7f-4b2c
Status: 429
X-Rate-Limit: tenant=1200rpm;window=60s
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
```
Not seeing spikes in token usage, mostly low token counts per request.

leo_infra: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) client heartbeat introduced synchronized fanout — many connections sending at same epoch boundary (rendezvous). 2) HTTP/2 stream parallelism combined with short requests can amplify request rate per connection.

maria_eng: Can you confirm if you use built-in retry jitter/backoff? If all clients retry in lockstep when they see 429 the second-order spike can look like repeating waves.

acme_ops: We had simple fixed 1s retry for instant failures — no jitter. Heartbeat interval is 60s exactly.

sara_support: Ok that helps. On our side I see tenant rpm peaked near the quota exactly at those windows and the rate limiter started returning 429s, then a bunch of clients retried quickly which produced repeated peaks.

replay_bot: Incident snapshot: tenant=acme-prod | peak_requests=1180rpm | quota=1200rpm | sustained_spikes_every=60s | distinct_client_ips=320 | avg_tokens=24

leo_infra: Repro plan: 1) run a short synthetic that mimics your heartbeat cadence with and without jitter, 2) enable client-side stagger (+random(0,5s)) and exponential backoff with cap, 3) if you need immediate relief we can temporarily bump the tenant RPM for 1 hour.

maria_eng: Also share a pcap or request timeline if you can. If heartbeats align to the top of the minute they can push you over the per-minute bucket even though per-second looks fine. Our limiter enforces rolling minute windows.

acme_ops: Quick timeline attached below (sanitized): 
```
10:02:59.980 -> 40 requests
10:03:00.010 -> 275 requests
10:03:00.300 -> 220 requests
10:03:00.900 -> 180 requests
10:03:01.200 -> 10 requests
```
Looks like alignment to the minute plus retries.

sara_support: That matches the rendezvous pattern. Two mitigation paths: client changes (preferred) or server-side smoothing. We can also enable a tenant-level "burst buffer" short-term bump while you roll out client fixes.

acme_ops: Timeline: can we get the buffer for 2 hours? Our rollout takes about 30 mins.

leo_infra: I can authorize a temporary +25% RPM for 2 hours. Will log the change and monitor. Please add a rollout plan for client jitter.

maria_eng: Recommended client changes: 
- heartbeat interval = 60s + random(0..5000ms)
- retries: exponential backoff starting at 200ms with random jitter, max attempts 5
- collapse duplicate heartbeats in the client (de-dupe per connection)

acme_ops: Implementing jitter now, pushing a config change in staging. Any guidance for measuring success?

leo_infra: After you deploy, run synthetic at production scale but with jitter enabled. Watch X-Quota-Remaining and our tenant metrics. Expect smoothing of peaks and no repeated 429s. We'll also watch for downstream load.

replay_bot: Post-change snapshot (simulated): peak_requests=900rpm | sustained=650rpm | 429s -> 0 in window sampled

acme_ops: Deployed jitter + backoff. Early results look good — no 429s for 30 minutes. Appreciate the quick help.

sara_support: Great to hear. Follow-ups: 1) keep the temporary RPM bump until your rollout is confirmed (leo will manage), 2) we recommend adding client telemetry showing next-heartbeat-delta to help detect alignment in future, 3) if you need long-term higher throughput consider Dedicated capacity or increasing quota via support request.

leo_infra: RPM bump expired but we kept an eye and no 429 resurgence. I'll close the temporary escalation ticket later today. :thumbsup: 

acme_ops: Thanks everyone :raised_hands: — will file a postmortem on our side about the fixed-retry anti-pattern and share learnings.

maria_eng: Great collaboration. Adding this pattern to our support runbook under "rendezvous/heartbeat fanout" with sample mitigations and a diagnostic checklist.

sara_support: Closing thread after confirming stability. If anything flares up reopen or ping #support. :white_check_mark:
